Some commits are single (atomic removals, docs, one build tweak). Your spec entry has a "slice" field: minimal | completion | single.

Historical commits are reference only; the final file is the fixed form.

SLICE SEMANTICS (critical -- this makes the series reviewable)
- slice=minimal: code genuinely does ONLY the small slice, and its test checks ONLY that slice. E.g. "Andes CSR drain+verify, min (mxstatus)" drains + verifies ONLY mxstatus (hand-coded, not the X-macro loop); "runtime crt0/UART, min" only makes vplat_hello print, no exit/file-io yet; "fixtures, min (one C fixture)" relinks ONE fixture. You author a genuinely reduced version, NOT the final file.
- slice=completion: expand the prior minimal slice to full final form and extend the test to cover all. After it, the touched file matches final MINUS still-later-feature parts.
- slice=single: author to final form minus later-feature parts, per construct. Removal commits ('refactor!: remove ...') delete the named subsystem.
- The construct field says exactly what reduced/full content to write and how to derive it from the final file.

INCLUDE/ SUBMODULE: at the ABI-pin commit (spec functionality abi-submodule, ~c010) replace the in-tree include/hybrid headers with the andesim_abi submodule using include_submodule_recipe: 'git rm -r' the in-tree headers, remove leftover include/, 'git -C /home/nick/work/andesim/include worktree add --detach /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim/include <v2 sha>', 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim add include' + the .gitmodules entry (copy from final tree). To advance the pin later (v3/v4/v5/v6 commits): 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim/include checkout <sha>' then 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim add include'. Never make include/ a plain tracked dir after that.

commit b86d168dcbd71d4dd5aacf3bd615cfc102a6dbe7
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 30 14:45:49 2026 +0800

    feat(run): hide vsim banner + [info] log; restate cycles as [andesim]
    
    Behavioral change. `run --mode cycle` ran vsim with inherited stdio, so the
    user saw vsim's startup banner (Copyright / Version) and its verbose [info]
    log mixed with the program's own output. Now cycle captures the engine's
    stdout+stderr line by line and presents a clean result: the program output,
    then the cycle count as "[andesim] N cycles". Dropped: the banner and every
    [info] line. Kept: real program output, real diagnostics ([warn]+), and the
    exit code. The "N cycles simulated" count is lifted from the [info] log (vsim
    --log-level can't help -- it also suppresses that line, and the banner is not
    log-level gated). fast keeps raw passthrough (QEMU has no such banner, and its
    monitor/gdbstub are interactive); cycle --gdb is interactive and unfiltered.
    
    Hybrid relayed its vsim leg's captured stdout, which carried the same banner;
    strip it there too (the leg's [info] is already absent -- its stderr is dropped
    at capture), so marker/pc results stand alone.
    
    The banner/[info]/count rule is a pure, unit-tested classifier (VsimFilter +
    parse_cycles_line; strip_vsim_banner is its buffer-mode form for the hybrid
    relay). run_line_filtered (process.cpp) is the streaming 2-pipe spawn behind
    cycle. The now-dead run_passthrough wrapper is removed: run_standalone builds
    the argv and branches between raw (exec_passthrough) and filtered
    (run_cycle_clean) presentation directly.
    
    Tests: new andesim-vsimfilter-test (pure classifier); f8 asserts cycle output
    is clean against real vsim (and its fake-engine cases now pass a real dummy ELF
    -- abs_elf rejects a non-existent path); f9 asserts the banner does not leak.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
